authoredFrom: Yul — Solidity's inline assembly, analysed as a first-class sub-language. Authored 2026-09-30 from the analyzer's measured output. The lane handoff said 'the corpus under-represents Yul' and proposed deciding whether to handle it or rule it out; the census REFUTED the premise (2,800 yul_function_call, 2,819 yul_identifier, 2,640 yul_path, 447 assembly_statement over the 389 production files), so ruling Yul out would have removed more edges than the entire contract layer's call graph. Building it in was the only defensible answer.
note: Yul variables and functions are contained by the Solidity FUNCTION that lexically encloses the `assembly` block, because the function is the nearest declaration container — Yul has no declaration of its own in the symbol graph's terms. `twice` is a Yul function: declared, given an owner, and called. `keccak256`, `shl`, `mstore`, `sstore`, `add`, `lt`, `gt`, `sub`, `iszero` are EVM OPCODES and are silent by SOL-8; the skip is lossless because the lexer always spells a bare `add` as the builtin, so a user-defined Yul function can never carry that name. `break` and `iszero(r)` inside the loop body are silent for the same reason.

forbidSymbols.comment: SOL-8: `add` is an EVM opcode (`yul_evm_builtin`), never a project symbol. The skip is lossless — the lexer always spells a bare `add` in Yul as the builtin, so a user-defined Yul function can never be named `add`.

expectRelationships.comment: A Yul `let` is a declaration, and its container is the enclosing Solidity function because the assembly block opens no declaration of its own.

Declared in the loop's INITIALISATION block. Yul has no block scope — a `for` initialiser variable is visible in all three blocks — so one declaration and one containment edge is the correct shape, not three.

A call to a Yul FUNCTION. `yul_function_call`'s `function:` field is `choice(yul_identifier, yul_evm_builtin)`, so a project Yul function and an EVM opcode arrive at the same node type and are separated by the node's own spelling — see the forbid rows for the opcode side of the same rule.

THE ROW THAT FOUND A REAL DEFECT. `yul_path`'s children are `yul_identifier`, NOT `identifier` — grammar.js declares `yul_identifier: $ => $.identifier`, an ALIAS, so the node type on the wire differs from the aliased one. Reading `identifier` children found none, the first Yul fixture emitted ZERO path reads, and 2,640 `yul_path` nodes in the corpus had never been read by anything.

The Solidity parameter read INSIDE assembly. A Yul frame does not stop a read of an outer Solidity binding, so the path read names it like any other. SUPERSEDED SPELLING (task-9 reconciliation, SOLIDITY-W8-CLAIM.md): this row pinned the BARE spelling of a function-scope binding read. The behaviour it pinned is now SUPERSEDED by the fleet binding claim (D7 CLAIMED, commit SOL-W8): a parameter/named-return read is published as `<declaring callable>\x00<binding name>` + metadata.localBinding, because the name has no published declaration and the bare spelling let the name-keyed resolver answer with a decoy. The construct the row tests is UNCHANGED — only its spelling moved. The old bare spelling is forbidden below so this fixture fails if the claim is ever removed.

The named RETURN variable, read and assigned inside the assembly. Solidity's named returns are real bindings and the assembly sees them. The construct the row tests is UNCHANGED — only its spelling moved. The old bare spelling is forbidden below so this fixture fails if the claim is ever removed.

A read of a Yul function PARAMETER, from inside the Yul function's own frame — so the scope is `twice`, not `compute`, AND the row is the family's BINDING spelling (W6-a): the parameter is a binding of the Yul frame and the family contract publishes no symbol for it. The bare row was the pre-fix shape and is forbidden below; a bare spelling would let the store resolve the read against whatever single declaration happens to carry the name.

forbidRelationships.comment: SOL-8: an EVM opcode is not a call. 2,800 such nodes exist in the corpus and none of them is a project function.
SOL-8. `keccak256` is a reserved grammar TOKEN and an EVM opcode; in call position the lexer spells it a bare `identifier`, which is why the derived ENGINE_FUNCTION_NAMES list exists at all.
SOL-8 on the read side: an opcode named in a `yul_path` is silent too, which is why the fixture asserts the count of `uses` rows rather than only forbidding these four by name.
A Yul block does not CONTAIN the Solidity parameters visible inside it — `x` is declared by `compute`'s signature and owned by `Assembler`. An assembly block is a scope, not a declaration container.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: Exactly ONE call in the file: `twice(…)`. Every other call-shaped construct is an EVM opcode (SOL-8), so a rule that did not separate opcodes from Yul functions would report 10, and one that separated them wrongly would report 0.
